## Tests: full headless sweep, runner stall guard, 81 tests moved to the native lane - October 12, 2026

Runner (`tools/run_tests.py`, c2761de1): a script error aborts a fixture's `run()` before its
`quit()`, leaving the process idle until the timeout. Once a `SCRIPT ERROR` has been printed and
nothing more arrives for 10 s, the test is stopped and reported `FAIL(hung)`. Verdicts are
unchanged (a script error was already a failure); a hung test costs about 15 s. The first sweep
without it took two hours for 105 of 456 tests.

Sweep of the headless lane (456 tests, six parallel workers, one scratch APPDATA each, about ten
minutes): 279 pass, 33 skip themselves as native, 144 fail (82 hung, 62 exited). Owner folder
unchanged. All 144 were then rerun with real windows on the second monitor:

- 65 pass with a window.
- 16 crashed headless on a missing image and run to a verdict with a window, still failing.
- 63 fail both ways with no missing-image crash.

Cause of the first two groups: `ImageTexture.get_image()` returns null under the headless dummy
renderer. Crew-storage frames decode their own pixels, so loader frames work headless, but a
test that injects a candidate manifest after the loader gets plain textures and crashes on
`get_image().get_data()`. Those 81 tests now have `lane: native` overrides with the reason in
`tests/index.json` (lanes: headless 375, native 529, skip 16). Checked through the runner: three
of them pass with `--native --screen 2` and report SKIP-NATIVE headless.

Still failing after this, by kind (lists in `output/full-suite-2026-10-12/`): {'Bill selected-art tests': 24, 'Bill candidate-art tests': 18, 'Bill other': 5, 'other crew art and animation': 7, 'not crew art': 9}.
The 16 that fail with a window are Bill meal, drink, inspect and seated candidate tests.
Not crew art: test_discovery_progression, test_hand_backdrop, test_inspector_refresh, test_large_room_art, test_learning_ui, test_research_tree, test_room_flooding, test_room_lock, test_staged_restore.
None of these were traced. The native lane (448 tests before this change) was not run.

Headless rerun of the 12 (`output/test-runs/20261012-202309-headless`): 8 pass, 3 fail, 1 times
out. Commits fe4f8577, 90bb64c8, bce9b016, 824a43dd, 8b002b00, 2080a50d. One game change.

the scene tree. Since crew storage (October 9) the crew loader ended with `Router.start(get_tree(),
...)` and the Bill loader returned early without a session, so the roughly 186 fixtures that call
them on a detached grid crashed or hung before their checks. Detached loads share one session
for the process (`_detached_crew_bank`); the in-tree game path is unchanged. Covered by
`tests/test_crew_loader_detached.gd` (16 checks: real main scene session, then two detached grids
in both loader orders). Adding a bare grid to the tree is not an alternative: its `_ready` needs
the whole game (about 90 errors, 11.7 s).

- test_crew_polish, test_crew_death_save: the "old checkpoint" fixture removed the engineer but
  kept `james_cargo_return`, which `james_cargo_checkpoint.valid_shape` rejects. Fixture now
  removes the record too.

  Now compares the gait fraction across the turn.

  rest family is 1.84 s and the game loader retimes those clips. Uses `Life.seconds` and the
  game's players. Bill's 8-frame clip then showed `frame_at_elapsed` landing one ulp short at

  expected the clock to carry over. Owner decision, October 12: a helmet change restarting the
  clip (`crew_sprite_player.frame`, `current_equipment`) is acceptable. Both now run separate

"waiting for passage". `scripts/crew_passage.gd` `try_yield` tested all 52 step-aside spots
for the blocker, each with a full `detour_around_crew()` for the mover: 4,992 route searches,
about 90 ms. None opened a route, and the whole sweep ran again on every frame with no pause:
351 consecutive steps and 1,752,201 searches in ten simulated seconds. This is the
"unexplained current-map simulation-step spike" from the October 11 handoff.

Fix in `scripts/crew_passage.gd`: a sweep tests `SPOTS_PER_STEP` (2) spots a step in the same
nearest-first order and continues on the next step; after a full sweep fails the pair waits
`RETRY_SECONDS` (0.5) of the mover's own traffic wait before sweeping again; a lower wait means
a new stand-off and starts fresh. Same spots, same order, same searches; only when they run.

- Same snapshot after the fix: worst crew step 106 ms to 6.7 ms, route searches 1,752,201 to
  17,356, passage step alone about 90 ms to about 3.5 ms, and the three actors end in the same
  places doing the same things.
- `tests/test_crew_passage_budget.gd` (+ UID, registered in the crew group): 15 checks on stub
  actors - per-step bound, every spot once per sweep, pause and retry, fresh start for a new
  stand-off, and a resolvable stand-off resolving at the nearest working spot. With the bound
  and pause switched off, 6 checks fail. `test_crew_spacing` and `test_battery_passage_probe`
  pass.

benchmark's `automatic_reports_saved: 1` in every packaged run is the same event. Not fixed;

use.

## Release: first versus second Continue explained; title-screen preload assessed - October 11, 2026

Measurement and code reading only; no source change. Same candidate and real Continue path,
reported save, with the loaders' own counters recorded (`continue-stats/`).

- First versus second start is the image prefetch list, not shaders or disk cache.
  `scripts/image_prefetch.gd` decodes on worker threads from `user://startup_images.txt`,
  recorded by the previous launch. Fresh profile: 13,312 image requests, 0 prefetch hits, 0
  worker submissions. Second start: 13,238 hits, 8.79 s of worker decode time, peak 247 MB
  decoded with the 96-image window. So the 12.3 s "first start" is a first launch after
  install (or after that file is lost), and 6.8 s is the ordinary case.
- Main-thread PNG time in the three-crew batch: 3.87 s on the first start, 0.36 s on the
  second. Frames loaded: Branforth 8,058, Veld 3,186, Marsh 1,190 (Bill separate), with 11,429
  registered frames discarded unused.
- On the second start the three-crew load is still 1.62 s and Bill 0.91 s although decoding is
  off the main thread: about 0.36 s PNG hand-over, 0.38 s waiting on compression workers, and
  the rest main-thread bookkeeping for that many frames.

Option 1 (start crew loading at the title screen), assessed:
- Not a simple move. The loaders are grid methods, store into grid fields, use the grid's
  texture pool and end with `Router.start(get_tree(), self, bank)`. Run as they are they would
  block the title screen for seconds.
- The prefetch cannot simply start earlier: it keeps at most 96 decoded images waiting for a
  consumer, and 13,000 decoded frames would be tens of gigabytes.
- What could work: prepare the compressed frame sources on worker threads at the title screen
  and hold them until the grid adopts them. `crew_storage/base_batch.gd` already skips decode
  and compression for a path whose source is alive. Estimated effect, not measured: first
  launch about 12.3 s to about 7 s; ordinary start about 6.8 s to about 5.8 s, because the
  main-thread bookkeeping remains. That clears the 10 s gate and leaves the 6 s gate marginal.
- Loading only the crew aboard (option 2) removes the three-crew load entirely when they are
  absent: about 1.6 s on an ordinary start and 4.75 s on a first launch, at the cost of loading
  a crew member when first met.

## Performance: gates scoped to real-size stations; lighting phase explained - October 11, 2026

Owner decision, October 11: the 60 FPS gates (p95 16.7 ms, p99 25 ms) apply to real-size
stations of about 12 rooms. The 38-40 room station is a stress test with a looser bar (no
reproducible stall over 100 ms). No source change in this entry.

Re-reading the same real-station runs (`real-stations-current-source/`, one run each, 4070 Ti):

- Steady play, idle and pan phases together (540 frames each): reported save mean 10.89 ms,
  p95 12.29, p99 15.84; frozen owner copy mean 10.71, p95 15.15, p99 22.66. Both gates pass.
- The lighting phase is slow because of the light fade, not a hitch. `RoomLighting.FADE_SECONDS`
  is 0.65 s; while a room's level moves, `scripts/grid_canvas.gd` repaints the floor,
  floor-rest, wall and light surfaces every frame (12 redraws instead of 8, drawing 8-10 ms
  instead of 3.5-4 ms). Frames during a fade: mean 17.89 / 15.96 ms, p95 20.89 / 19.62. Frames
  after it settles match idle. The benchmark flips interior lights once a second, so about
  three quarters of that phase is inside a fade; normal play fades only when power or lights
  change.
- The zoom phase changes zoom twice a second and has p95 17.5-17.7 ms for the same reason:
  it is a stress pattern.
- Not explained: on the owner copy, a few idle/pan frames at 2x and 4x speed reach 17-36 ms
  with drawing time up to 28 ms and no upload or extra redraws. They do not break p99.

Nothing was changed for the fade: making it cheaper without altering its look or timing has no
known exact method. Remaining release risk is no longer pacing on this PC but the unmeasured
targets (GTX 1650-class PC, M1) and the packaged-build certification list in the handoff.

## Performance: where frame time goes, real stations re-measured - October 11, 2026

Measurements only; no source change. Diagnostic runtime with current normal source mounted,
effect and cargo storage on, one run each, RTX 4070 Ti. Not release certification.

- Real stations, 1080 frames each, 12 phases: reported save (12 rooms) mean 12.54 ms, p95
  18.34, p99 21.55, max 24.1, none over 25 ms. Frozen owner copy (10 rooms) mean 12.03, p95
  17.39, p99 23.37, max 42.3, 8 frames over 25 ms, none over 50. So p99 passes its 25 ms gate
  on both and p95 misses 16.7 ms by 0.7-1.6 ms. The lighting phases are slowest (mean
  14.3-16.5 ms); idle is 10.0-10.4 ms. Evidence: `real-stations-current-source/`.
- Mixed-large stress station (38 powered rooms): idle frame 26.1 ms = 12.0 ms grid drawing
  callbacks (37 canvas redraws a frame), 7.8 ms render boundary, 2.2 ms simulation step, about
  4 ms not covered by the trace. Real stations idle: 3.6-3.9 ms drawing (8 redraws), 3.1-3.5 ms
  render. Roughly 0.6 ms of frame per extra room on this machine.
- Texture uploads are zero in a typical idle frame. Rover body and wheel uploads were 460 ms of
  32,719 ms in the stress run (1.4%); owner chose not to crop body sheets.
- Large-room base drawing, labelled per room (`large-base-attribution/`): Moonbay 1.85 ms a
  frame plus 0.31 ms live gates while its mission runs; Tidal 0.26 ms; Hydroponics Farm and
  Storage Depot about 0.02 ms each. The October 8 private Tidal static-layer candidate would
  therefore save at most about 0.26 ms here; not integrated.
- Layer alignment probe (scratch): layers cropped to one shared area match each other exactly
  (120 of 120); a layer on its own tight area differed from the shared one in 4 of 120. Whole
  rover through `drone_animation.gd` draw, cropped cargo against full sheet: 130 of 150 zoom
  and position cases identical, 331 pixels differ in the other 20, 19 of them at a half-pixel
  position. `output/cargo-on-rover-comparison-2026-10-11.png`.

## Performance: cropped mining cargo storage integrated, Windows-guarded - October 11, 2026

Owner decision, October 11: cropped cargo storage is accepted although scaled drawing is not
byte-identical. They reviewed `output/cargo-crop-comparison-2026-10-11.png` first. Correction
to what that review was told: the drawn outline can shift by one row or column, not only
interior rows. Uncommitted.

- Why: the eight collect/unload cargo sheets upload 96.3 MB each while the cargo covers about
  27x165 of each 448x448 frame. Stored cropped they decode to 2.3-2.7 MB per sheet.
- `scripts/drone_animation.gd` draws each cargo frame from its own small texture, uploaded the
  first time that frame is drawn, using the same full-frame quad. Supported context: nearest
  filtering, repeat disabled, no material or the flood material. Anything else, an edited
  original, or missing/invalid storage draws the original sheet.
- Guard: `cargo_storage_enabled` is true on Windows only, off with `--reference-cargo-storage`.
- New: `scripts/drone_cargo_storage.gd`, generated `scripts/drone_cargo_storage_catalog.gd`,
  eight sheets under `assets/mining-rover-v1-2026-09-26/cargo-storage/`, generator
  `tools/build_drone_cargo_storage.py` (`--check` verifies every visible pixel reconstructs and
  everything outside the kept area is transparent), `tests/test_drone_cargo_storage.gd`
  registered native under gameplay.
- Acceptance rule in the test: unscaled drawing at a whole-pixel origin is byte-exact (plain,
  alpha, tint, flood). Scaled drawing: every drawn pixel must be a source pixel within half a
  source pixel of where the full sheet samples. Measured: 716 of 95,460 scaled pixels (0.75%)
  take the adjacent source pixel, none anything else.
- Verified, scratch APPDATA, secondary monitor, muted: cargo test 274 checks, 0 failures, and
  96 failures when the frame is deliberately offset two pixels. Effect storage, invisible
  cache, upload diagnostics and session art cache pass native; eight headless drone and
  reliability tests pass. Owner folder fingerprint unchanged.
- Matched normal-source pair (mixed-large, 1080 frames per lane, 12 of 12 states and cameras
  exact, 328 cropped-frame draws, 0 fallbacks): cargo upload work 1026.8 MB / 105.8 ms to
  562.9 MB / 67.8 ms; all upload time 753.1 to 682.6 ms. Peak texture counter unchanged
  (2744.336 to 2744.384 MiB). Mean 30.341 to 30.296 ms, p95 45.640 to 46.014, p99 53.975 to
  56.308, max 96.133 to 78.184, frames over 50 ms 24 to 19. One pair: no pacing claim.
  Evidence in `cargo-storage-normal-integration/` under the benchmark-input-isolation folder.
- Limit of this result: the workload touched only three of the eight sheets, once each. The
  remaining large uploads in it are rover body sheets (101 uploads of 40 MB or more, 545 ms)
  and the eight 48 MB carry-cargo sheets, which are not cropped yet.

Next candidates, not started: carry-cargo sheets (same method), the east mining effect sheet
and sixteen single-colour construction effect sheets (exact two-channel storage), and whether
rover body sheets can be cropped. Pacing gates and full PC/Mac certification remain open.

## Latest implemented work

- Routing and crew spikes (Sept 26), measured on the saved seed-73 47-room station

  (`expedition-73-progressed-known-recipe-final/latest.loop`; its `final.loop` is gone):

  - Swim smoothing retries keeping the search's facings, so a shortcut can no longer

    strand a graph-valid escape. The Sept 23 doorway report now escapes in ~25 ms

    (was: no escape, 153–262 ms per retry, 740 ms worst update).

  - Every crew spike was a goal choice. Smoothing shortcuts reach two rooms; the swim

    A* uses a heap (identical costs on 40 real pairs); a failed swim search skips

    proven-unreachable targets within one choice. 30 cycles: worst 389 → 143 ms,

    slow frames 11 → 5, mean 5.3 → 3.6 ms.

  - Corridor swim clearance skips sampling when the body is inside a proven floor

    rectangle: cold failing swim search 820 → 481 ms, all 23,444 link answers unchanged.

  - Swim-to-walk routing (owner approved): crew swim or walk per room, so a swimmer's

    route now plans dry rooms with the walking check (`swim_cells`, published by

    `room_flooding.advance`; no map = old swim-everywhere planning). Branforth, stuck

    in the flooded reactor because the crew hab's furniture blocks a swim outline, now

    reaches a bunk in 17 s. 30 cycles: worst frame 143 -> 115 ms, mean 3.4 ms.

  - Crew stand-offs (fresh seed-101 review run): two crew meeting in a doorway tried a

    detour from every start in the room, each a failed search (269 starts, 500 ms,

    repeated per step-aside spot: 1 s frames). One fill from the target now predicts

    reachable starts (0 mismatches vs the real search at 26 stand-offs); detour

    smoothing got the two-room reach. Stand-off frames 1,018 -> 53-79 ms.

  - The seed-101 review run (alive at cycle 173, Veld rescued) froze from cycle 29:

    mining exhausted, and the test player waited forever for metal. Test-player limit,

    at first; the rerun (test player now rerolls unaffordable cards) reached metal 0 and

    showed a **real zero-metal softlock**: once surveyed deposits are gone there is no metal

    source (orbit rewards exist in `orbit_manager.gd` but nothing calls `orbit.advance`).

    Fixed per owner choice: BRINE Core reclaims +1 Metal every 3 cycles while Metal < 2 and no

    bay can harvest (`scripts/metal_trickle.gd`), and any leaf room can be scrapped from the

    inspector for half its Metal (`scripts/room_scrap.gd`; not the core, wards, crew habs,

    occupied rooms or rooms others need to reach the core). Rerun: metal recovers to 2 and

    corridors keep extending.

  - Room completion hitch: every crew member rebuilt navigation and re-chose its goal in one

    frame (141-176 ms on the 47-room station). The main crew loop now rebuilds one crew member

    per frame (`defer_navigation_rebuild`); peak 33-64 ms.

  - `test_marsh_expedition_presentation` failed about 1 run in 3: its route clearing erased

    unidentified ("recovery") wards when the random site put one on the route, so the saved

    site was invalid and the checkpoint read fell back to its backup. It now keeps them;

    the failing seeds 1, 6 and 11 pass and 8/8 random runs pass.

    The first run's `final.loop` was deleted by a probe (restore points

    autosave at the source file); events, profile and screenshots remain.

  - Bunk: the seated frame sits on the mattress edge. Colour-matching the bunk art and

    smoothing crew sprites were tried and reverted (props v2 doc, Open).

- `test_owner_report_regressions` passed only with the owner's saved Studio layouts:

  its flooded-escape fixture started on a corner node. It now starts where the swimmer

  fits and passes with default and owner layouts. (`test_room_catalog_cards` failed once

  in a busy isolated run and passed 3/3 after; not layout-dependent.)

## Workflow

Follow the repository's two pipeline skills and [workflow guide](ASSET_PIPELINE_AND_WORKFLOW.md).

The [bible](BRINESPACE_VISUAL_AESTHETIC_BIBLE.md) owns art direction and

[release workflow](RELEASE_WORKFLOW.md) owns packaging. Read relevant development

notes before gameplay changes. Search scripts/rooms/tests/tools/docs/assets with

bounded paths; avoid recursive output/ scans. Preserve frozen saves and use disposable

copies for Continue/conclusion. Wait for observable startup, inspect error logs,

and run only appropriate validation. Update this summary at the next real milestone.
